summary: Skewed short/long request mix triggering amplified flushes in continuous batcher causing intermittent p95/p99 surges
description: Customer BeaconAI reports intermittent increases in p95 and p99 inference latency for their dedicated pool. Spikes appear as short-lived waves (5-20 minutes) where p99 climbs from baseline ~200ms to 1200-1800ms and some requests time out. Affected traffic pattern is a skewed mix of very short single-turn prompts and occasional long multi-turn streams that resume KV cache usage. Suspected tie to continuous-batcher flush behavior under asymmetric sequence-length distributions.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use BeaconAI ded pool in us-east-1 and replay a trace with 85% short (<=8 tokens) single-request calls and 15% long (>=512 tokens) streaming sessions interleaved.
2) Observe request latency distribution in metrics/per-tenant dashboards.
3) Look at continuous-batcher flush_size/flush_interval and per-tenant queue depth.
4) Re-run with only short requests or only long requests as control; spikes do not reproduce consistently outside mixed workload.

investigation_notes:
Observations: (a) p99 correlates strongly with spikes in inter_batch_interval_p99 and spikes in small flush_size counts (many small micro-flushes followed by large flush) rather than steady batch sizes. (b) Tenant queue depth oscillates: short request bursts reduce linger, triggering early micro-flushes; long streams later cause larger batches that stall GPU worker for longer and amplify downstream queueing for short requests.
Hypothesis: Continuous-batcher adaptive policy uses recent mean sequence length and queue depth to decide linger. Under rapidly changing short->long mixtures this control loop under- or over-shoots, producing a resonant effect: clusters of small flushes then a large flush that creates head-of-line blocking and inflight KV cache warmups, causing 5xx/timeouts.
Also observed increased CPU steal on a subset of GPU nodes (host-7a, host-7b) coincident with spikes; possible noisy-neighbor exacerbation.
Data/metrics checked: per-tenant flush_interval histograms, per-connection latency traces, gpu_utilization, host_cpu_steal, kv_cache_miss_rate, request_size_percentiles.
Preliminary root-cause: control-loop oscillation in adaptive linger combined with mixed short/long sequence workloads and occasional host resource contention.
mitigation_and_workaround:
1) Temporary per-tenant override pushed: set tenant.batch_override.max_linger_ms=6 and tenant.batch_override.disable_cross_tenant_coalesce=true for BeaconAI — deployed 2026-03-12T14:05Z.
2) Rerouted a fraction (10%) of BeaconAI traffic to an isolated dedicated subpool to limit noisy neighbor effects.
3) Encouraged customer to smooth request pattern if possible (short-request batching window).
Effect: within 10 minutes p99 dropped from ~1450ms to ~240ms and error rates returned to baseline. Monitoring continues.
resolution:
Workaround applied and holding. Long-term fixes proposed: (A) Update continuous-batcher control loop to incorporate sequence-length variance and add anti-resonance jitter in linger adaptation. (B) Add per-tenant detection that automatically applies short max_linger for high short/long variance workloads. (C) Investigate node-level scheduling to reduce CPU steal/noisy-neighbor exposure for dedicated pools.
Owners: serving-runtime (PR GH#12860) for algorithm change, infra scheduler for host placement. Targeted rollout: canary 2026-04-02, full rollout 2026-04-16. Follow-up task INT-4189 created for scheduler investigation.
